busy: Reading the address from its chain's indexer. A busy address takes a little while.
checked: Checked: dealings with labelled exchanges, flagged addresses and mixers, use of the same address on several EVM chains, and who sent the address its first coins on each chain. Only addresses in the label sets can be recognised, so no finding is not a clean bill.
empty: No address to scan. Paste an EVM, Solana or Tron address into the scanner.
error.title: The scan did not finish
evidence.title: What the findings rest on
finding.x-exchange-exposure.description_: {{count}} transfer went between this address and {{exchange}} on {{chains}}. The exchange knows that this address belongs to one of its customers, and can be made to say who.
{{count}} transfers went between this address and {{exchange}} on {{chains}}. The exchange knows that this address belongs to one of its customers, and can be made to say who.
finding.x-exchange-exposure.recommendati: Treat this address as known to the exchange. Keep funds that should stay apart from your identity away from it, and withdraw to a fresh address rather than to this one again.
finding.x-exchange-exposure.title: Dealt directly with an exchange: {{exchange}}
finding.x-flagged-counterparty.descripti: {{count}} transfer with an address labelled as a scam, a hack or under sanctions. Exchanges can freeze or question funds that touched such an address.
{{count}} transfers with addresses labelled as a scam, a hack or under sanctions. Exchanges can freeze or question funds that touched such an address.
finding.x-flagged-counterparty.recommend: Keep these funds apart from the rest, and be ready to explain where they came from if an exchange asks.
finding.x-flagged-counterparty.title: Dealt with a flagged address: {{name}}
finding.x-funder-exchange.description: {{exchange}} sent this address its first coins on {{chains}}, the gas it started with. The exchange knows that this address belongs to one of its customers, and can be made to say who; anyone who looks at its first transaction sees the withdrawal too.
finding.x-funder-exchange.recommendation: Treat this address as known to the exchange from its first transaction. A wallet that should stay apart from your identity should not get its first coins straight from an exchange withdrawal.
finding.x-funder-exchange.title: First funded by an exchange: {{exchange}}
finding.x-funder-hub.description: {{funder}} sent this address its first coins on {{chains}}, and also sent coins to {{wallets}}. It is too busy to be one person, or known as a service: most likely an exchange or a payout service. So it is not taken as a link between your wallets; it still knows where it sent the coins.
finding.x-funder-hub.recommendation: If you know who it is, label it in the app. If it is an exchange, the exchange knows that both wallets belong to its customers.
finding.x-funder-hub.title: First funded by a busy address that also funded {{wallets}}
finding.x-funder-mine.description: Your wallet {{funder}} sent this address its first coins on {{chains}}. Anyone who looks at its first transaction ties the two together, and whatever is known about one then applies to the other.
finding.x-funder-mine.recommendation: Fund a wallet you want kept apart from your others from a source that does not lead back to them.
finding.x-funder-mine.title: First funded by your wallet {{funder}}
finding.x-funder-shared.description: {{funder}} sent this address its first coins on {{chains}}, and also sent coins to {{wallets}}, which you track as yours. It was read and is not busy, so it looks like one person: wallets funded by the same person are the first thing a Sybil hunter groups together.
finding.x-funder-shared.recommendation: If this address is a service you know, label it in the app. Otherwise treat these wallets as tied together, and fund the next one from a different source.
finding.x-funder-shared.title: Funded by the same address as {{wallets}}
finding.x-mixer-counterparty.description: {{count}} transfer with a labelled mixer. Its use is public, and exchanges often flag funds that passed through a mixer.
{{count}} transfers with a labelled mixer. Its use is public, and exchanges often flag funds that passed through a mixer.
finding.x-mixer-counterparty.recommendat: Expect questions when these funds reach an exchange. A mixer only hides the path when its deposit and withdrawal cannot be matched, by amount or by timing.
finding.x-mixer-counterparty.title: Dealt with a mixer: {{name}}
finding.x-multi-chain.description: This address is active on {{chains}}. Whatever ties it to a person on one of them ties it on all of them.
finding.x-multi-chain.recommendation: Use a separate address on each chain whose activity you want kept apart.
finding.x-multi-chain.title: The same address on several chains
gap.skipped: A check ran out of calls and did not run: {{check}}.
gap.truncated: The address is very active: only its newest transactions were read.
